tagline: A possibly Lombard-origin tower that gave its name to "la Berardenga" — a self-catering Chianti estate on the medieval Siena-Florence frontier
highlights: A tower of possible Lombard origin (6th-7th century), one of Chianti's oldest elements
Major strategic importance between the 13th and 15th centuries on the Siena-Florence frontier
The Hall of Arms preserves frescoes depicting estate life under the Palmieri family
description:
Most of Montalto Castle is of medieval origin, with some parts predating the 11th century. The tower was probably built by the Lombards in the 6th or 7th century, but the castle's main body was constructed toward the end of the first millennium by descendants of Winigi, first Salic count of Siena under the Franks in the 9th century, and of his son Berardo, from whom the Berardenga region takes its name.

The fortification held major strategic importance between the 13th and 15th centuries because of its border position between Siena and Florence. Various restoration works were carried out in the 16th and 19th centuries. When peace returned to Tuscany under Medici rule, Montalto lost its brief independence, and descendants of the Palmieri transformed it into a country residence, decorating the Hall of Arms with frescoes depicting life on the estate.

The tower's possible Lombard origin, if accurate, would place Montalto among the older fortified sites in the Chianti region, predating the more commonly documented Sienese and Florentine medieval castle-building of the High Middle Ages.

The estate's namesake connection to Berardo, son of Siena's first Salic count, ties Montalto directly to the origin of "la Berardenga" as a named historical region — an unusually direct link between a specific castle and the place-name of its surrounding territory.

The castle's border position between Siena and Florence during the 13th-15th centuries gave it genuine strategic value during exactly the period when these two republics were most aggressively contesting Tuscan territory, a role it lost once Medici rule pacified the region.

The surrounding Chianti Classico wine route and the town of Castelnuovo Berardenga give guests staying at Montalto easy access to one of Tuscany's most established wine-growing traditions.
history: Montalto Castle has parts predating the 11th century, with a tower of possible Lombard origin and a main body built toward the end of the first millennium by descendants of Winigi, first Salic count of Siena, and his son Berardo, namesake of the Berardenga region. It held major strategic importance on the Siena-Florence frontier between the 13th and 15th centuries. Once Medici rule pacified Tuscany, the Palmieri family transformed it into a country residence, decorating its Hall of Arms with frescoes of estate life.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Montalto Castle within the castle building itself?
faqs.answer: No — the estate's 21 rooms (up to 43 people) are split between the castle itself and historic houses surrounding it on the same property. Confirm whether your booking is in the main building or one of the annex houses.

faqs.question: Why is this castle called "Montalto in Chianti" instead of just "Montalto"?
faqs.answer: "Montalto" is a very common Italian place name — Montalto delle Marche, Montalto di Castro, and Montalto Uffugo are among several other Italian localities with their own castles. Anchoring the title to "in Chianti" avoids that ambiguity.

faqs.question: What does the Hall of Arms at Montalto Castle depict?
faqs.answer: Frescoes showing life on the estate under the Palmieri family, added when the castle was converted from a fortified border post into a country residence.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 20 minutes from Siena and 1 hour from Florence by car; Florence's Peretola Airport (FLR) is about 1h10. A rural area — a car is recommended.

**Rooms & rates:** 21 rooms (up to 43 people), split between the castle itself and historic houses surrounding it on the same estate. From €194/night (low-season rate for the smallest unit).

**On-site:** Hall of Arms with historic frescoes, gardens, self-catering estate.

**Good to know:** As a villa/self-catering estate with houses around the castle, confirm whether your booking is in the main building or one of the annex houses.

**Combine with:** Siena (~20 min), Castelnuovo Berardenga and the Chianti Classico wine route, Florence (~1h).
